messages:
Alex: Quick note — after yesterday's kernel swap I see a regression on long sequences in the replay harness, ~12% p99 increase for 8k seqs when using the FUSED_ATTN kernel vs BASELINE. Has anyone else seen a similar delta?
Maya: I noticed something like that in my run. My hypothesis: batching heuristic + KV warmup interaction. Replay has a heavy tail of long seqs, so continuous batching groups short requests and the long ones pile up -> p99 jump.
Alex: Repro config (snippet):
```
harness:
  mode: replay
  sample_rate: 0.25
  seq_bins: [64,512,2048,8192]
  kv_warmup: on
  kernel_override: fused_attn
```
Maya: Watch out — with sample_rate < 1 the per-client KV mapping can diverge and you get inconsistent cache warmup across runs. For apples-to-apples we need deterministic KV state or sample_rate=1.
Ben: For consistent comparisons we should: 1) set sample_rate=1 or synthesize same seq distribution, 2) pin kernel selection, 3) clear KV or run a fixed warmup window between runs, 4) run >= 30 iterations and report median/p95/p99. Also log GPU utilization.
Riley: Profiled a failing run — flamegraph shows `kv_cache_lookup` ~35% stalls and `fusion_kernel_setup` ~28%. Looks like lookup latency + kernel prep overlaps poorly with batching. Suggest trying shard-level batching or limiting max_batch_size.
Alex: I reran with sample_rate=1 and explicit KV flush between runs. p99 improved but still ~9% higher vs baseline; TPOT dropped as well. Quick metrics CSV: QPS=480, goodput=410, TPOT_p50=22ms, TPOT_p95=68ms, TPOT_p99=130ms, TTFT_median=7ms.
Maya: Quick defs for the thread so we don't mix terms: TTFT = time from client send to first token out. TPOT = time from request start to final token out. p95/p99 are tail latencies. QPS = raw requests/sec. Goodput = tokens/sec that meet our latency SLO (e.g. p95 < 100ms) — i.e., effectively useful throughput. Make sure harness emits tokens_emitted and tokens_late to compute goodput.
Ben: We also need to separate cold vs warm KV in reporting. Proposal: test matrix = {cold (KV flush), warm (15min prewarm replay), mixed (50/50 skew)} and run each scenario. That way we can see how kernel choices behave under different cache regimes.
ci-bot: run complete — artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/1745016789-report.html :white_check_mark:
Riley: Agreed on matrix. Also add GPU metrics: GPU_util%, SM_active%, mem_bw, and avg_batch_occupancy. Without those we can't normalize across instance types.
Alex: Next steps: I'll open a PR with a canonical bench config that enforces sample_rate=1 for replay apples-to-apples runs, explicit KV control (flush/prewarm), pinned kernel, and the metric output fields (TTFT, TPOT p50/p95/p99, QPS, goodput, GPU%). We'll add a short checklist for regression runs.
Maya: If you add regression detection to CI, add a baseline tag and a guard that alerts on >5% p95 regression and optionally auto-rollback if regression persists across N runs.
Ben: :thumbsup:
Maya: Also consider a micro-benchmark that isolates `kv_cache_lookup` and `fusion_kernel_setup` latency (single-request stress with varied batch sizes) — that'll help prove cause vs correlation.
Alex: Good call. I'll include a tiny micro-bench harness in the PR too. Thanks all.
